prompt:
Create a grayscale 3D character construction reference sheet for Akinza, a fully fur-covered fictional animal creature. Image 1 supplies the character identity, face and overall proportions. Image 2 supplies only the approved tail shape: three thick round tails with pointed ends, meeting together directly at a compact base where they join the lower back. Image 2's simple block body is only a placeholder.
Show exactly three complete figures, clearly separated and labeled FRONT, LEFT PROFILE, BACK, on a white landscape page. Same character, same neutral upright technical stance, same scale, consistent proportions. Arms relaxed slightly away from body, feet planted slightly apart. No props or dramatic acting.
Preserve huge broad sideways ears with soft shaggy fur borders, large distinctive oval eyes, small nose, short feline muzzle, slender furry torso and limbs, small clawed paws and broad furry feet. Keep a simple streamlined lower torso. Show soft gray sculptural volumes with broad simplified fur masses instead of dense hair texture. The character remains fully covered in fur.
Make head depth, short muzzle projection, neck connection, shoulder and limb volumes, ankle and paw connections legible. Ears are shallow cupped flexible forms, thin with a soft rounded rim and furry edge, attached high on the sides of the head. In profile they foreshorten rather than keeping full frontal width.
Tail shape follows IMAGE 2 rather than the earlier tail in IMAGE 1. Three full rounded unequal tails taper to points, fuse directly together at their compact body attachment, and extend toward the creature's own left and slightly backward. No projecting central stalk, no delayed trident split, no flat feather or leaf shapes. Front view shows tails to viewer right, back view shows tails to viewer left. Left profile faces viewer left; the sideways tail sweep foreshortens toward the camera, with modest rearward projection to viewer right.
Soft neutral shading, level orthographic-style cameras, aligned head heights and ground lines. These are proposed design studies for a later actual model. Prioritize recognizable identity and readable whole-body construction.
verdict: Whole-body direction retained except tail root, rear contours and gaze. Profile projection and digit inconsistencies block geometry use.
